description:
FOUND by the s509 review of s507p (Fable's table; reproducer ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s509/review/sb/sb.pl app-match 30000): a regex ANCHORED AT THE END of a string that grows by .= costs a scan from the string's START on every iteration, so append + match per iteration is QUADRATIC -- on main and on the s507p tree alike.  NOT the string-buffer work: a plain LEXICAL scalar (no buffer cell, no snapshot) shows it too.

Reproducer (s507p worktree: scratch/s507p/probes/appmatch2.pl SECTION N):
  my %h; my $m = 0; for my $i (1 .. $N) { $h{u} .= "line $i\n"; $m++ if $h{u} =~ /9\n\z/ } print "$m\n";

Measured 2026-10-06 08:22 (load ~8, wall incl. start-up); pcl = s507p tree bc276159, base = main fee16466:
  section                                N=10000   N=20000   perl N=20000
  match    ($h{u} =~ /9\n\z/)             2.17 s    8.34 s    0.03 s   (base 2.39 / 8.26)
  lexmatch (my $u =~ /9\n\z/)             1.34 s    5.54 s             (base 1.44 / 5.14)
  substr   (substr($h{u}, -2) eq "9\n")   0.28 s    0.84 s             (base 0.27 / 0.90)
THE DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT: the same loop with substr(-2) in place of the match is ~10x faster, and the lexical spelling (no cell at all) is as quadratic as the element one -- so the cost is the regex engine, not the read of the string.  (The substr row's own residual growth is #2722, a snapshot per read of a buffer cell.)  Review table at 30000: perl 0.09 s, main 11.05, tree 10.80.

Suspect to measure first: perl starts an end-anchored match (\z, \Z, $) near the end of the string (its minlen / anchored-at-end check); PCL's engine tries every start position from 0.  Cheap test that confirms or kills it: time /9\n\z/ against /x\z/ (never matches) and against a one-shot match on a 1 MB string; if the one-shot is linear in the length and ~N/1 start positions are tried, the suspect is confirmed.
Filed only (s507p); owner: the regex engine.

=== DESIGN (s512, Fable, 2026-10-07) -- THE SUSPECT IS CONFIRMED and the fix is measured; perf round 41 member 1 ===
MEASURED (probes endanch2.pl, ppcre-end*.lisp in the s512 scratchpad; results in PAUSE-s512.md): a ONE-SHOT match of /9\n\z/ on a 4 MB string
costs PCL 9.8 ms (hit) / 33 ms (miss, /x\z/) and 8 ms at 1 MB -- LINEAR in the length, so the engine tries every start position from 0;
perl 0.3-0.8 us.  A string built by 1000 appends costs the same as one built by `x`, so it is not the copy and not the buffer cell.
cl-ppcre 2.1.2 ITSELF (the vendored copy, called directly): "9\n\z" 36-40 ms, "x\z" 27-29 ms, even the unanchored constant "a9\n" 36 ms --
its end-string / end-anchored optimisation (api.lisp create-scanner-aux, scanner.lisp) is NOT in effect for these patterns
(end-string NIL); the START-anchored one is ("^9" 0.05 ms, "\Ax9" 0.000 ms).
THE FIX, measured on cl-ppcre directly: call the scanner with :start = len - L and *real-start-pos* = the ORIGINAL start:
"9\n\z" 0.000 ms, "x\z" 0.000 ms, "\b9\n\z" (no match, right), "(?<=x)9\n\z" (match, right), "^9\n\z" (no match, right -- ^ anchors
to the real start).  *real-start-pos* is what cl-ppcre's anchors, \b and lookbehind read (closures.lisp 157/164/291/355/367:
`(or *real-start-pos* *start-pos*)`), so binding it to what the scanner would have seen as *start-pos* keeps every anchor's
meaning while the scan LOOP starts at the tail.
SHAPE (one place, no call-site change): in %pcl-build-scanner, after the scanner is built, compute from the pattern's PARSE TREE
(`cl-ppcre:parse-string` of the normalised pattern; public API) whether the pattern is END-ANCHORED -- the top-level :sequence
(through :group / :register / :flags wrappers) ends in :modeless-end-anchor-no-newline (\z; newline allowance 0),
:modeless-end-anchor (\Z; allowance 1) or :end-anchor ($; allowance 1, and ONLY when no multi-line mode is in effect: the
:multi-line-mode option or a (:flags :multi-line-mode-p) anywhere in the tree makes $ match before any newline -> no optimisation) --
and its MAX match length L (characters): :sequence = sum, :alternation = max, repetition = max * len(x) when max is a number
else UNBOUNDED, string = length, character / :everything / any char class / :property = 1, :word-boundary / anchors / lookahead /
lookbehind / :flags / :void = 0, :register / :group / :standalone / :branch / :filter / :regex = inner (a :filter with no length,
a :back-reference = UNBOUNDED).  When end-anchored AND L is bounded, return a WRAPPER closure of the SAME signature
(str start end) that does (let ((cl-ppcre::*real-start-pos* (or cl-ppcre::*real-start-pos* start)))
(funcall scanner str (max start (- end L allowance)) end)); otherwise the scanner itself.  Both the ordinary and the MINEND
variant (%pcl-build-minend-scanner: a zero-width :filter appended, L unchanged) get it; the cache (*pcl-scanner-cache*)
memoises it.  Every call site (%p-ppcre-scan, %p-global-scan, the anchored-list scan, s///, split) is unchanged.
GUARD ROWS (perl-probed, in the round's Pl/t/perf-levers-09.t + a semantics file): fixed length (/9\n\z/, /\.$/ with and without
a trailing newline, /\Z/), bounded (/\r?\n\z/, /(a|bcd)\z/, /x{2,5}$/), UNBOUNDED (/\s+\z/, /;\s*$/ -- no change), /m with $
(no change), \b and lookbehind at the tail, ^...\z on a 1-char and an empty string, a /g scalar loop with pos() past the tail
start, s/x\z/y/ and s/\n\z//, split /\n\z/, captures' positions (@- @+) after the wrapper, a match on a string shorter than L,
a tied / overloaded subject, the minend variant (`while ($s =~ /x*\z/g)` terminates).  Bench: a new tools/bench-exec.pl row
`endanch` (append a line and test the tail, 30 000 times: perl 0.09 s, main 11 s) and the s509 review table re-taken.
subject: A regex anchored at the END (/X\z/) of a string growing by .= scans from the start on each match: append + match per iteration is quadratic (main and s507p alike; 8 s vs perl 0.03 s at 20k)
